proposals.observation: The Daily Blog Post GitHub Actions workflow failed at 10:05 on 29 August. There is only one post queued and 47 published, meaning the pipeline is effectively stalled. No quiz sessions have started in 48 hours, and no new signups are recorded — a broken publish workflow is the most likely single point of failure suppressing all downstream metrics. The Funnel-Hack Digest also failed the same day, suggesting a shared dependency (likely an API key, a Node version mismatch, or a broken import) rather than two unrelated faults.
proposals.proposal:
Open the Daily Blog Post workflow file and inspect the failing step. The two same-day failures point to a shared environment issue — check for an expired API key secret (e.g. OPENAI_API_KEY or MAILERLITE_API_KEY) or a Node version that drifted after a runner update. Once identified, either rotate the secret in GitHub Settings > Secrets, or pin the node version in the workflow to the last known-good value. This is the highest-leverage fix available: nothing else compounds until content is publishing again.

Note: the blocked-paths rule prevents Fred from writing directly to .github/workflows/*. Joel must apply this fix manually. The file path below is given for navigation only, not for automated commit.
proposals.new_text:
# Manual fix required — Fred cannot commit to .github/workflows/*
#
# Likely causes (check in this order):
#
# 1. Expired or missing secret.
#    Go to: GitHub repo > Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions
#    Verify OPENAI_API_KEY and MAILERLITE_API_KEY are present and not expired.
#    Rotate if needed, then re-run the failed workflow manually.
#
# 2. Node version drift.
#    If the runner recently updated, pin the version explicitly:
#
#    - name: Set up Node
#      uses: actions/setup-node@v4
#      with:
#        node-version: '20'
#
# 3. Broken import after a dependency update.
#    Check the full failure log for "Cannot find module" or "SyntaxError".
#    If found, pin the offending package in package.json to its last working version.
#
# After fixing, re-run both "Daily Blog Post" and "Funnel-Hack Digest" workflows
# to confirm the shared root cause is resolved.

proposals.impact: capitalise on 66.67% open rate with stronger CTA to discovery call
proposals.observation: The Money Vigilance automation has a 66.67% open rate across 12 sends — well above the other two sequences. Money Vigilance subscribers are already the most engaged cohort in the list. If the first or second email in that sequence does not contain a specific, grounded invitation to book a discovery call, that engagement is leaking out without converting.
proposals.proposal: Add a single plain-text paragraph at the close of the Money Vigilance sequence's first conversion email. The paragraph should name what Money Vigilance actually costs a person at Joel's ICP age range (watching the account grow while life expenses pile up un-examined), then offer the discovery call as a concrete next step. Avoid any structure that reads like a pitch; keep the register quiet and direct, consistent with the sequence's existing tone.

proposals.impact: surface quiz entry point to drive first quiz sessions from existing traffic
proposals.observation: Zero quiz sessions in 48 hours despite the quiz being live. The homepage (index.astro) is the highest-traffic page on the site and is almost certainly receiving visitors — the quiz is simply not being reached. Either the quiz link is not visible above the fold, or the current homepage copy does not give a person a reason to start it. With no new signups recorded and no funnel activity, restoring quiz traffic is the fastest route back to list growth.
proposals.proposal: Locate the primary hero section of the homepage. Replace the current call-to-action button label and the single sentence immediately above it. The new sentence should name a specific feeling that Money Vigilance, Money Avoidance, and Money Worship subscribers have all demonstrated they recognise ("earning steadily and still not building anything") rather than a generic invitation. The button label should say what the quiz actually does, not what it promises.
